svg.text: B-C KOLBENSTRANG — food as a plug in a pigged tube
Food sits in an open tube with a free piston; a press pushes the plug through an exchangeable die and a wire cuts it off.
press 450 W × 600 D, closed yoke for 10 kN
die pressure 10.5 bar at 10 kN · grid 1.9–4.8 kN
FRONT VIEW (press frame, cartridge carousel, die turret)
pan / pot / Buch-Wender mat / baking dish
two silicone lips wipe the wall on
two cartridges mouth to mouth: 8 kN = 8.4 bar,
≈ 36 passes of 5 s = 3 min (unproven for gluten)
One press replaces dicer, ricer, former, Spätzle press, pump
Weak: does not wash, peel, toss, whip or coat; hard produce needs up to 10 kN.
Best used as the forming and metering station inside another concept.
1/8 At LOAD a cartridge (open tube with a free piston) is filled with meat mass through the funnel.
2/8 The carousel turns the cartridge under the press; the die turret has the open ring ready.
3/8 The ram pushes the piston; the plug comes out of the ring and the wire cuts a patty every 15 mm — into the pan.
4/8 Next cartridge (a peeled onion, root down) to the press; the 12 mm grid is indexed under it.
5/8 The onion is pushed through the grid, the blade cuts every 6 mm: regular 12 × 12 × 6 mm dice.
6/8 Next cartridge: boiled potatoes, skins on; the 3 mm ricer die.
7/8 Ricing: mash falls into the pot, the skins stay on the die; the piston wipes the bore clean (pigging).
8/8 Cleaning: tube, piston and die are three open parts — they go to the ware washer; the ram never touched food.
